# stackit_observability_http_check (Resource)

Observability HTTP check resource schema. HTTP checks are unique per URL within an instance: creating a check for a URL that already exists returns the existing check. Two resources with the same `url` therefore manage the same check, and destroying one of them deletes it. Must have a `region` specified in the provider configuration. This service is only available when the provider is configured with `default_region = "eu01"`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stackit_observability_http_check" "example" {
  project_id  = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
  instance_id = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
  url         = "https://www.example.com/healthz"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The Observability instance ID to which the HTTP check is associated.
- `project_id` (String) STACKIT project ID to which the HTTP check is associated.
- `url` (String) The URL to check.

### Read-Only

- `http_check_id` (String) The HTTP check ID.
- `id` (String) Terraform's internal resource ID. It is structured as "`project_id`,`instance_id`,`http_check_id`".

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [` + "`" + `import` + "`" + ` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the ` + "`" + `id` + "`" + ` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Only use the import statement, if you want to import an existing observability http check
import {
  to = stackit_observability_http_check.import-example
  id = "${var.project_id},${var.observability_instance_id},${var.observability_http_check_id}"
}
```
